subject: Human Evolution
title: Skin Color and Sunlight
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Skin Color and Sunlight.

hook.text: Near the equator, skin is dark. Near the poles, it's light. This gradient maps perfectly to UV intensity.

buildup.text: UV light destroys folate, a vitamin essential for fetal development. Dark melanin blocks UV.

discovery.text: But UV also triggers vitamin D production. In low-sun regions, lighter skin absorbs more UV for vitamin D.

twist.text: Skin color is a balancing act: too much UV destroys folate; too little UV blocks needed vitamin D.

climax.text: Human skin color is a textbook case of natural selection adapting the same species to different climates.

punchline.text: Skin color is geography, written in melanin.

quiz.question: Why does skin color vary by latitude?
options: A trade-off between UV protection (folate) and vitamin D production
